narrative.overview:
Talky looks like a part of the Mac. Every Talky surface is one material, glass, floating over one ground: a deep navy-to-indigo color field lit by three soft lights. The download page, the onboarding window, the Settings header band and the floating pill all use this same field and this same glass, so the product reads as one object wherever it appears. The world refuses the category default of a flat white page with a screenshot; retro and physical-object styles were also rejected.

The mood is calm, dark and lit from within. Density is low: large bold headlines with tight tracking, plain body text at a generous size, and capsules of glass for everything that can be pressed. Depth comes from blur, a thin white rim and a top specular line, not from heavy shadows or ruled boxes. Violet, blue and peach exist as light in the field, not as paint. The solid accents are few and each has one job: the white primary button, the selection blue, the live red.

One world, two platforms. The web draws glass with CSS backdrop blur and saturation. The app draws it with native Liquid Glass on macOS 26 and later, and with the ultra-thin material plus a light rim on macOS 14 and 15. In the app, system controls (pickers, toggles, secure fields, the Settings sidebar) keep their native styles; the world lends type, palette, glass and the pill.
keyCharacteristics: One color field behind every Talky-world surface; glass is the only material on top of it.
White ink on dark glass. Secondary text is white at reduced opacity, never a gray.
Capsules for anything pressed or floating alone; rounded rectangles for containers.
SF Pro only, bold and tightly tracked at display sizes.
The pill, with its numbered pipe chips, appears on every surface.
Red means one thing: the microphone is live.

rules.name: The One Field Rule
rules.body: Every Talky-world surface sits on the same field: a navy, indigo, deep-field gradient (160° on the web, top-leading to bottom-trailing in the app) lit by violet at the top right, peach at the lower left and blue from below. The radial light is the ground of the world, not an accent glow. On the web the field is fixed behind the page and its three lights drift slowly (38 s, 46 s and 52 s, alternating); with reduced motion they stand still. The lights burn at full strength only behind the first screen: within the first 160px of scroll they fade to 55% (`--glow`), so text set directly on the field keeps at least 4.5:1 over their brightest point. On phones the peach light sits lower (top 60vh), behind the Notes window, not behind the small print. Both values were measured, not guessed; re-measure before raising either.

rules.name: The Light, Not Paint Rule
rules.body: Violet, blue and peach are light inside the field. On glass surfaces they never become text, button fills, borders or card tints.

rules.name: The Live Wire Rule
rules.body: Live Red appears only while the microphone is live: the pill's recording dot, which pulses. Still previews, buttons, badges and errors never use it.

rules.name: The Blue Means Chosen Rule
rules.body: Selection Blue marks the selected pipe and the action that moves forward. It is never decoration.

rules.name: The Platform Voice Rule
rules.body: SF Pro is the only family, on both platforms. No second display face, no webfont.

rules.name: The Tight Top Rule
rules.body: Bold display type tracks tighter as it grows: -0.02em to -0.035em on the web, -0.4pt to -0.6pt in the app. Body text never tracks below -0.01em.

rules.name: The Steady Numbers Rule
rules.body: Numbers that change or line up use tabular figures: the pill timer and every key badge.

rules.name: The Fixed Slot Rule
rules.body: On the web the pill sits in a 272px slot, right-aligned against the chips and as wide as its Listening state, so the chips never move when the pill changes state. Below 760px the slot spans the row and centers the pill.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: Both Settings pages pad their content 20pt on every side. The header band, the groups and the pipe rows share those column edges, so changing pages never shifts the layout. General stacks its groups 26pt apart; Pipes stacks its parts 16pt apart and its pipe rows 12pt apart. In the header band the title sits left and the pill preview right; when the window is narrow the pill moves under the title.

rules.name: The Soft Shadow Rule
rules.body: Drop shadows are long and blurred. No hard, zero-blur offset shadows. The 1px inset specular line at the top of glass is part of the material, not a shadow to remove.

rules.name: The Deep Glass Rule
rules.body: Reading text in a panel sits on deep glass, never on light glass: a navy-indigo fill from 46% at the top to a 42% floor behind the text. The floor keeps white text at 4.5:1 over the peach light. The demo window may fade its fill to 14% only below the text, so the field shows through the empty part. Light glass is for chrome and controls: the nav, buttons, the pill, chips and key caps.

rules.name: The Veil Rule
rules.body: Native glass that floats over other apps (the pill, its chips, the processing and message capsules, the transform picker) carries the navy tint inside the glass and the navy veil over it. Liquid Glass turns light over white documents even when tinted; the veil keeps white text readable. Glass inside Talky's own windows, which always sit on the field, uses a black 15-18% tint and no veil.

rules.name: The Two Layers Rule
rules.body: Dictation and pipes are separate layers, and every surface shows them in that order. Dictation is free, on the Mac and needs no key. Pipes need an Anthropic key. Pipe chips appear only where pipes are explained or turned on.

rules.name: The Way Forward Rule
rules.body: Every onboarding state has a visible way forward, and the primary button names what it does with what the user entered. A button never says "Skip" for something the user just typed.

rules.name: The Nothing Fake Rule
rules.body: In onboarding, anything that looks like a control works. A still pill looks pressable, so onboarding shows none: the welcome explains the hotkey with a key cap and icons, and the first real use is the Try it step.

rules.name: The Idle Preview Rule
rules.body: Every still picture of the pill shows the idle state: a white 50% dot, "Hold fn" (or the user's hotkey), no waveform, no red. The red dot belongs only to a pill that is actually recording, or to the web demo while it runs.

dos: Do put every Talky-world surface (the web page, the onboarding window, the Settings header band, pill previews) on the one color field.
Do put reading text in panels on deep glass with its 42% navy floor; keep light glass for the nav, buttons, the pill, chips and key caps.
Do draw native glass through the shared glass modifier: Liquid Glass with a tint on macOS 26 and later, the ultra-thin material with a 22% white rim and a soft shadow before that.
Do add the navy veil to any native glass that floats over other apps.
Do show the idle pill in every still preview.
Do keep the web pill in its fixed 272px slot so the chips never move.
Do keep the filler strike: mark "um", "so" and "like", strike them for 900 ms, then fade and settle.
Do keep both Settings pages on the shared 20pt column, with the header band on top and Settings groups below.
Do leave native controls in their system styles; in Settings the field stays inside the header band.
Do stop the field drift, the caret blink and the settle animation under reduced motion.
donts: Don't use Live Red for anything except the dot of a live microphone.
Don't use hard, zero-blur offset shadows.
Don't put reading text on light glass or on a fill below the 42% deep-glass floor.
Don't use violet, blue or peach as text, fills, borders or card tints on glass surfaces; they are light in the field.
Don't use the field's radial lights as glows on cards or buttons.
Don't add a second typeface or a display font; SF Pro is the voice.
